subject: Quick pulse on Ember AI discovery + internal pre-bump alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@ember.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@ember.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed next steps (Redwood x Ember)

Matthew / Sara — great speaking today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

TL;DR: Ember is evaluating hosted inference for a customer-facing feature (low-latency text generation at scale). Priority: product-launch window in Q3, procurement expected in mid-June pending SOW & security review.

Key notes from our call:
- Target workload: 50–100 qps with occasional bursts to 300 qps; typical prompt length ~120 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: PII filtered at source; still need confirmation on retention policy and encryption-at-rest requirements.
- Success signal: <100ms 95th percentile latency for single-region API calls; cost target ~0.0005 / token.

Proposed next steps (today -> two weeks):
1) I’ll share discovery notes (attached) and a short Redwood 1-pager on performance profiles.
2) If useful, book a short SE deep-dive to validate latency targets (30–45m).
3) Sara / Matthew to confirm timing for security/compliance kickoff and list of stakeholders (infosec + procurement).

Calendar: https://calendly.com/marcus-redwood/ember-follow-up
Attachments: ember_discovery-notes-20270510.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up in a week if I don’t hear back.

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

Thanks Marcus — brief thoughts from SE side before you bump: 

Suggested bump tone: short, helpful, and offer a low-effort win (SE review session). Script bullets:
- Quick reminder of the product-launch timeline and why we think Redwood helps (latency + cost control).
- Offer a 30m technical review with proposed agenda (latency validation, caching options, deployment modes).
- Attach a short latency-profile example and a templated SOC2 checklist excerpt (these are lightweight and often unblock procurement).

Technical talking points to include (1–2 lines each):
- Autoscaling behavior during burst traffic and warm-up strategies.
- KV cache / prefix caching options that reduce token usage for repeated prompts.
- Model fallback plan to maintain availability if a preferred variant has capacity issues.

I’ve attached a one-pager we can include. If Marcus wants to send the bump, happy to join the follow-up call.

—
